title: Would you trust an AI-generated stock market signal?
author: ClaimSignificant9189
selftext:
I’ve been running an experiment with an AI system that continuously analyzes stocks, market momentum, news, catalysts and potential early breakout setups.

I recently opened a small public part of it:

[https://www.dokai.fi/aistocktrading/](https://www.dokai.fi/aistocktrading/)

The goal isn’t to generate endless “BUY AAPL” recommendations.

I’m more interested in whether AI can combine multiple weak signals — unusual momentum, volume changes, market regime, news catalysts and price structure — and identify potentially interesting situations *before* the crowd has already moved the stock.

The system also tracks its own mistakes and tries to learn which types of signals actually worked.

It’s experimental, and the signals should absolutely not be treated as financial advice.

For those of you who actively follow stocks:

**What would an AI have to show you before you would consider one of its signals useful?**

Confidence? Historical hit rate? Price target? Catalyst? Volume confirmation? Something else?

Would love some skeptical opinions.

comments.author: fluffymeowmeowkitty
comments.body: Problem is you don’t set a goal for ai.   Like tell it what you want to achieve. Then give you recommendations.   In what universe does it live and what does it need to filter out?
